evals.name: plain-readme
evals.prompt: Can you turn the README at evals/fixtures/plain-readme.md into a nice PDF I can share with the team? It's the readme for our parqet CLI tool. No diagrams in it, just headings, an options table, and a couple of code blocks.
evals.expected_output: A designed A4 PDF in the default light theme rendered from the parqet README: a cover from the title, sectioned prose, the options table styled, and the install/usage code blocks syntax-highlighted. No content runs off the page.
assertions: A light-theme PDF was produced (light is the default; the request did not ask for dark, so no dark PDF is required).
Each PDF is a valid, non-empty PDF that opens and has at least one page.
No content is clipped or runs off the page edge on any page in the theme(s) rendered.
Output looks intentionally designed (cover/title treatment, clear section hierarchy, consistent styling) rather than a raw markdown dump.
The options/flags table renders as a real styled table with all its rows and columns intact.
The install and usage code blocks render as syntax-highlighted code blocks (monospaced, distinct from body text).
[with_skill only] The authored pdf.tsx imports only from '@engineering/using-doc-creation' with no relative imports or local asset files.

evals.name: mermaid-spec

evals.expected_output: A designed A4 PDF in the default light theme where both mermaid diagrams render as actual vector diagrams fully inside their cards (nothing clipped), the prose is sectioned, and the retry/backoff content reads cleanly. No overflow.
assertions: A light-theme PDF was produced (light is the default; the request did not ask for dark, so no dark PDF is required).
Each PDF is a valid, non-empty PDF that opens and has at least one page.
No content is clipped or runs off the page edge on any page in the theme(s) rendered.
Output looks intentionally designed (cover/title treatment, clear section hierarchy, consistent styling) rather than a raw markdown dump.
The delivery flowchart appears as an actual rendered diagram (nodes and arrows), not as a code/text block and not a blank box.
The sequence diagram appears as an actual rendered diagram (participants and messages), not as code and not blank.
Both diagrams sit fully inside their cards/containers with nothing clipped at the card or page edge.
[with_skill only] The authored pdf.tsx imports only from '@engineering/using-doc-creation' with no relative imports or local asset files.

evals.name: markdown-mermaid-spec
evals.prompt: Can you turn evals/fixtures/mermaid-spec.md into a Markdown doc I can drop into our wiki? It should render on GitHub with nothing installed — I don't want a PDF, just clean portable Markdown. It has two mermaid diagrams (a flowchart and a sequence diagram); keep those as diagrams.
evals.expected_output: A single plain-GFM Markdown document (no build step) covering the webhook delivery spec: a title, sectioned prose with headings, and the two mermaid diagrams preserved as ```mermaid fenced code-blocks (NOT rasterized to images and NOT dropped). No embedded HTML/CSS styling, no callout/badge/card markup — just portable Markdown.
assertions: The output is a Markdown document (not a PDF and not a pdf.tsx / React file).
It is valid, portable GitHub-Flavored Markdown: headings, and prose, that would render on GitHub with no build step.
Both mermaid diagrams are present as ```mermaid fenced code-blocks (the flowchart and the sequence diagram), not rasterized images and not omitted.
No section of the source spec is dropped — the retry/backoff delivery content is all represented.
The document contains no embedded HTML/CSS and no ShadCN-style callout/badge/card markup — it is plain Markdown only.
[with_skill only] No pdf.tsx was authored and no PDF was rendered for this request — the Markdown format needs neither.
